text:
ArtCraft Launcher 

 
 One place to install, update and open every app in the Craft App Suite, rebuilt in pure Rust. 
 PhotoCraft, LightCraft, FilmCraft, DesignCraft, VectorCraft, PdfCraft, EffectCraft, AniCraft, WordCraft, 
 DeckCraft, GridCraft, CADCraft, SoundCraft, FigCraft, Craft Anything, TextureCraft, MaterialCraft and the community apps SolidCraft and MailCraft: the right build for your computer, kept up to date.
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 Download ArtCraft Launcher ·
 ArtCraft ·
 The Craft App Suite 
 

 [!NOTE]
 ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life. Painters, photographers,
 filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil
 last week. If you make things, you're one of us. Come say hi on Discord. 

 
 What it does ·
 Features ·
 Downloads ·
 Build from source ·
 Craft App Suite ·
 Discord 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 Switch between the grid and a sortable table. 
 

 What it does

The Craft apps each ship their own builds for every platform. ArtCraft Launcher saves you from
hunting through a dozen release pages: it lists every app in the suite, shows which ones you have
and which version, installs the right build for your operating system and processor, and tells
you when an update is out. It is a small native app that can sit in your menu bar or system tray.

 Features

 
 
 
 📦 Install in one click 
 Picks the right download for your OS and CPU (DMG, MSI, AppImage, .deb, .rpm and more), checks it against the release's SHA-256 checksums and installs it.
 
 
 🔄 Stay up to date 
 Checks each app's GitHub releases and updates the ones you have. A notification tells you when there's something new.
 
 
 🧭 Always at hand 
 Opens any Craft app from one window, or from the tray and menu-bar icon. Native egui, no Electron, no web view.
 
 
 

The Fonts page is Craft Font Manager: browse the Google Fonts and Noto collections (and index
URLs you add), preview families in their own faces, and install them into the font store every Craft
app reads. Font files download only after you allow font downloads in Settings or confirm an
install. Previews come from a font preview server; Settings can change the server or turn previews
off.

The web version shows the same catalog in the browser, with the latest download for each app; the
Fonts page is desktop only.

 Interface languages

The interface is in English, Bosnian (Bosanski), Brazilian Portuguese (Português (Brasil)), Czech
(Čeština), French (Français), Georgian (ქართული), German (Deutsch), Hungarian (Magyar), Japanese
(日本語), Polish (Polski), Russian (Русский), Simplified Chinese (简体中文), Traditional Chinese
(繁體中文), Spanish (Español) or Ukrainian (Українська). Auto , the default, follows the system or
browser language; Settings → Language picks one and switches at once, and the choice is kept
between runs. Bosnian locales ( bs , bs-BA , bs BA.UTF-8 …) select Bosnian, Czech ones ( cs-CZ ,
 cs CZ.UTF-8 …) Czech, Georgian ones ( ka , ka-GE , ka GE.UTF-8 …) Georgian, German ones ( de-DE ,
 de-AT , de-CH , de DE.UTF-8 …) German, French ones ( fr-FR , fr-CA …) French, Hungarian ones
( hu , hu-HU , hu HU.UTF-8 …) Hungarian, Japanese ones ( ja , ja-JP , ja JP.UTF-8 …) Japanese,
Polish ones ( pl , pl-PL , pl PL.UTF-8 ) Polish, Ukrainian ones ( uk , uk-UA , uk UA.UTF-8 …)
Ukrainian, Spanish ones ( es-ES , es-MX , es-419 …) Spanish, and Portuguese ones ( pt-BR , and
 pt-PT too, for now) Brazilian Portuguese. Simplified Chinese locales ( zh-CN , zh-SG , zh-Hans ,
and POSIX forms such as zh CN.UTF-8 ) select Simplified Chinese; Traditional Chinese ones ( zh-TW ,
 zh-HK , zh-MO , zh-Hant , and POSIX forms such as zh TW.UTF-8 ) select Traditional Chinese, with
an explicit script winning over the region. To try a language without changing the setting, start
the desktop app with ARTCRAFT LAUNCHER LOCALE=pt-BR , or add ?lang=ru to the web address.

The CJK languages are drawn with the system's own CJK font (Hiragino Sans or PingFang on macOS,
Yu Gothic, Meiryo or Microsoft YaHei on Windows, Noto Sans CJK, IPA, Takao or WenQuanYi on Linux and
FreeBSD); Traditional Chinese prefers an installed Noto Sans CJK TC, then PingFang TC, Microsoft
JhengHei or MingLiU. Georgian is drawn the same way, with the system's Georgian font (SF Georgian or
Arial Unicode on macOS, Sylfaen on Windows, Noto Sans Georgian or DejaVu Sans on Linux and FreeBSD).
Where the system has no font for one, and in the web version, the interface stays in English and
Settings says why. Product names and release notes stay as published; text without a translation
falls back to English. See docs/localization-zh-hant.md for the
Traditional Chinese catalog and font details.

 Where apps are installed

ArtCraft Launcher installs each app where your system normally keeps applications, using the
app's official release package, so an app installed by the launcher is the same as one you
installed by hand (and the launcher finds apps you installed yourself):

 System Where How 
 --- --- --- 
 macOS /Applications/ .app Copied from the signed, notarized release DMG 
 Windows C:\Program Files\ArtCraft\ ( Program Files (x86) for a 32-bit build) The release MSI, through Windows Installer, for everyone on the computer (with Start menu entry and Apps & features entry). Windows asks for administrator permission for each new install. An app already installed for your account only ( %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ArtCraft\ ) keeps its folder and scope when updated; to move it, uninstall it and install it again 
 Linux /usr/bin , /usr/share/applications The release .deb (apt) or .rpm (dnf, zypper), with your system's password prompt. Without those, a Flatpak, or an AppImage in /Applications 
 Linux, inside the launcher's Flatpak, with no Flatpak on the host /.var/app/ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher/data/artcraft-launcher/apps/ The release tarball, unpacked into the launcher's own folder and run inside the same sandbox, with its settings in a home/ folder beside it.

install.title: Installing your own builds
install.html:
To install and update the Craft apps from checkouts on your machine instead of GitHub, clone them next to this repo (../photocraft, ../wordcraft, …) and run:

cargo xtask local sync      # git pull every app, build and package each new version into ../local-mirror
cargo xtask local serve     # serve the builds and a release feed on http://127.0.0.1:8787/
ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_DOWNLOAD_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8787/ cargo run --release -p artcraft-launcher --features local-mirror

Run sync again whenever you want updates, or let the server do it: cargo xtask local serve --sync-every 1h pulls and builds on that interval while it serves. An app is rebuilt when its checkout's version isn't in the mirror yet (--rebuild forces it), and the launcher's next check picks it up. Add --every-commit to build every new commit instead, as a dev version between releases (0.4.0 builds as 0.4.1-dev.<commit time>), which the launcher offers as an update. While ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_DOWNLOAD_BASE is set (loopback addresses only), the launcher asks only the mirror, never GitHub. Only builds with the local-mirror feature read it; releases never have it. cargo xtask local help lists the options (--only, --no-pull, --arch, …).

New contributors and AI agents: start with AGENTS.md. Release packaging lives in packaging/ and .github/workflows/release.yml.

[!IMPORTANT] Status: ArtCraft Launcher is new and in early alpha. Expect rough edges, and please file issues (include your OS, which app you were installing and the launcher's log file) or tell us on Discord.
